nodes.label: UX & visual program (2026-07 audit follow-up)
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Built from 12 screenshots across every core flow, seven dimension reviews against the code, and three adversarial critique passes. Of 51 findings, 3 were killed as duplicates, ~12 revised, and 3 disproven against the code. Seven independently shippable workstreams; four audit items conflicting with settled decisions are held for an explicit owner call.

nodes.label: Workstream A — quick wins batch
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: 16 unanimously-endorsed fixes, but explicitly NOT 16 commits: the 2026-07-27 interaction audit found A4+A5 rewrite the same panel blocks (separate commits guarantee conflicts) and A12 makes a hint pill appear in states many specs click through. Commit shape is ~10, ordered so hit-area padding (A13) applies once to the final button set.

nodes.label: A1 — Escape mid-round records the run
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: The Escape exit handler called endGame() + writeIdleHash during playing and city round-ended, so the score was never shown and the personal best never recorded — while the HUD End-game button correctly routed through finishFree. Routing those Escapes through finishFree aligns the two paths; game-over Escape keeps endGame because finishFree is a no-op there and the hash must reset.

nodes.label: A13 — 44px touch-target convention
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Sheet header buttons ~36px, search-clear ~24px (the WCAG 2.5.8 floor exactly) and HUD text buttons ~16px (below even that floor) get padded hit areas to >=44px on touch surfaces without changing glyph sizes. The convention is pinned by a unit test in the layoutConstants style rather than left as a review habit.

nodes.label: A8 — stray clicks stop destroying comparisons
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: With compareWith set, a click on a third country fell through to select() and tore down the pair. Reinterpreted: third country replaces B, clicks on A or ocean are no-ops. Descoped to map-click semantics with a four-case e2e matrix; the border-chip-per-column clause moved to workstream C, which rebuilds those columns. Must resolve the interaction with the click-origin mark, since a replace-B click now feeds preserveZoom into the compare camera path.

nodes.label: Workstream B — a political map that shows its politics
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: The default satellite view hides every basemap label, so a political world map shows no country names at any zoom, and the vector view is dominated by roads and admin-1 labels in one AA-failing gray. This is the 'batch 3' political-legibility cycle batch 2 anticipated — pursued through labels, cased borders and a selection spotlight instead of per-country fill tinting.

nodes.label: B1 — app-owned country labels on satellite
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Glyphs decided and live-verified: text-font ['Noto Sans Bold'] via the positron style's existing glyphs endpoint, which stays loaded because satellite is a raster layer inside the always-loaded positron style, not a style swap. One cached ~77 KB PBF covers all 249 Latin-1 names, so no font assets ship and no bundle-budget change is needed. Self-hosting brand-font PBFs is rejected because the glyphs URL is style-global in MapLibre 5. Game gating needs a new explicit rule (visible iff satellite && !hideLabels) because the visibility owner deliberately skips custom country-* layers. E2E asserts seam visibility only, never rendered text, since the tile stub serves empty glyph PBFs.

nodes.label: B2 — cased country borders on satellite
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: A cased pair (dark casing under a light line) via the single paint owner, which batch 2 already taught to write border width per mode. The cased resting state supersedes batch 2's satellite-play emphasis branch — the values are near-identical, so the gameActive branch and its truth-table rows are retired and play and rest render the same borders.

nodes.label: B3 — vector political mode pass
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: A layer-id matcher demoting roads and admin-1 boundaries and restyling symbol layers by tier. The program's one real drift-risk item because it depends on third-party style layer ids, so it is severed from the B tranche and safe to slide or cut. Tested against a committed style-JSON snapshot fixture (no network in npm run check) and must fail open at runtime — unmatched layers stay positron-default, never broken. No scheduled fetch job; fixture refresh is a documented manual step.

nodes.label: B4 — selection as spotlight, not sticker
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Selecting France covered it with 0.32-opacity fill, making the requested country the least legible thing on screen. Inverted: a country-dim layer filtered to everything EXCEPT the selection (and compare partner), selection fill dropped to <=0.10, tighter glow. Load-bearing invariant: every queryRenderedFeatures call in app and e2e code is layer-scoped today, which is the only reason a new fill layer cannot pollute click handling or ocean-click preconditions.

nodes.label: B5 — reveal fill pulse
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: A dedicated country-reveal-fill layer rather than a borrowed selection layer — the single-owner lesson. Test contract: map paint animation is invisible to Element.getAnimations, so the waveform is unit-tested and e2e polls the settled fill-opacity through the map seam instead of data-animation-state.

nodes.label: B6 — compare camera via asymmetric padding
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: A screen offset cannot fix zoom sized to the full viewport, so country B still slid under the panel; asymmetric cameraForBounds padding replaces the mechanism while keeping batch 2's behavior contract. The wide-pair midpoint fallback and globe-scale guard encode live findings and are kept until the padding approach passes the same live cases.

nodes.label: Workstream C — a compare view that actually compares
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Each column rendered fields conditionally, so rows misaligned when one country lacked a value and compare silently dropped Timezones and Independent. One shared field-definition array drives desktop grid and mobile list, with paired bars scaled to max(A,B) and delta chips for numerics, and identical categorical values collapsed into one centered row.

nodes.label: Workstream D — a panel that answers 'so what?'
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Hero stats with world ranks computed from the in-memory 195-country dataset (zero data cost); attribution collapses 11 hover-only, tabIndex=-1, keyboard-unreachable per-field rings into one Tab-reachable footer that expands to the full field-to-source table, preserving granularity one interaction away.

nodes.label: Workstream E — Observatory visual identity
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Direction chosen by the owner on 2026-07-27 from a three-option review (Night Atlas / Observatory / Expedition Ledger). The globe is the observed object and the chrome a calibrated instrument. Deliberate trade-off: the 'fun' in funworldmap lives in copy and game feedback, not the hue system — if the live pass reads cold, the correction is copy and motion, not new hues.

nodes.label: E4 — two-accent semantic color tokens (ice / signal)
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Two accents with one meaning each: ice = interactive and wayfinding; signal = live game state and loss. Coral retires; teal migrates to ice. Region badges and A5's exception badges are explicitly outside the system — they are data encodings, not chrome accents. Shipped as its own atomic tranche (~92 teal occurrences across 29 files) so users never see a mixed-accent state.

nodes.label: E2 — typographic roles and the readout face
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Data readouts move to the system mono stack at zero bundle cost. Known risk: ui-monospace resolves to different faces per OS, so layouts must not depend on exact glyph widths — tabular alignment within one platform is the guarantee, not cross-platform pixel parity. Most surfaces already set tabular-nums, so .text-readout is a face change rather than an alignment fix.

nodes.label: E5 — landing behavior: derived center + idle rotation
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Initial longitude derived from Intl timezone via a static table — no geolocation, no network. Both the derived center and the rotation are disabled under VITE_TEST_HOOKS because host timezone varies between dev machines and CI and camera-dependent specs scan around viewport center. Rotation stops permanently on first interaction, pauses when the document is hidden, and self-stops after ~120s; the recurring cost is the WebGL render loop, not tile fetches (the z1.8 world pyramid is a few dozen cached tiles), recorded so the CDN-churn question stays answered.

nodes.label: E8 — instrument chrome grammar
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Corner-tick frames and tight radii are reserved for data surfaces (stat readouts, launcher cards, HUD badges); overlay shells keep the soft-radius backdrop-blur grammar. One boldness locus — the readouts — and everything around them stays quiet.

nodes.label: Workstream F — game feel
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Three reduced-motion-gated CSS-only HUD beats each exposing data-animation-state per CLAUDE.md; no libraries, no emoji. Retention comes from personal bests plus F2's share loop rather than a reinstated daily.

nodes.label: F2 — game-over recap and copy-result share
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Adds history: RoundOutcome[] to the reducer so the overlay can list per-round outcomes, with missed entries clickable into that country's panel — game to lookup, the product's core loop. Copy-result uses navigator.clipboard.writeText, which is safe; only readText is banned per project memory.

nodes.label: F3 — region filter as the difficulty lever
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: No separate difficulty system — region IS the difficulty lever, and 'Africa only' is the stated educator use case. Personal bests key per (mode, region) extending the v2 key scheme, explicitly applying the v1 daily-pollution lesson. CountryLike must gain region, which it does not carry today.

nodes.label: F4 — round-start camera ease to world view
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Amends the 2026-07-10 'carry-over is intended difficulty' call on the audit's friction evidence (target Bangladesh, camera parked over Europe — 2-4s of pan/zoom chores per round). Easing to a fixed world zoom while keeping the current center makes the globe reachable in one click without hinting at the target. Test contract changes from 'no move at all' to 'no move toward the target'; e2e waits on !map.isMoving() because camera moves are invisible to Element.getAnimations.

nodes.label: Workstream G — mobile platform feel
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: G1 ships sheet fundamentals (dvh, safe-area padding, one grabber implementation D4 consumes). G2 pointer-drag with snap points is deferred as the riskiest e2e surface in the program, needing its own data-animation-state design. G3 recomputes the camera offset from the actual snap fraction, since panelScreenOffset bakes in the collapsed height only.

nodes.label: Tranche sequencing and pre-agreed cut line
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: E-foundations is pulled forward as its own atomic tranche so C2's compare bars truthfully match already-migrated map fills. A cut line is pre-agreed (B3 -> G4/E7 -> E5 -> F3 -> D3 -> E-remainder) with a named floor that still honors the audit, and no tranche starts before its predecessor's review closes — the program is seven plans, not one.

nodes.label: Seam-based contracts for map paint and camera animation
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: DOM animations expose data-animation-state, but map paint and camera animations are invisible to Element.getAnimations, so they use unit-tested waveforms plus e2e polling through the map test seam — never hand-timed attributes. Reinforced by CI-coverage honesty: 13 of 38 specs are local-only, so axe and animated-path coverage holds only at the local merge-time run.

nodes.label: Owner decisions of 2026-07-27
nodes.author: Tobias Ens (with Claude)
nodes.rationale: Round-start camera change approved (ships as F4); light-theme top strip accepted as intended under the space-dark constraint; the shipped timezone '+N more' toggle stays; the daily challenge stays removed, with the date-seeded mechanic recorded only in case the decision is ever revisited.

edges.source_location: Relationship to prior specs — the daily stays removed
Amends the camera rules in exactly three places
A1 — route playing and city round-ended Escapes through finishFree()
A13 — pin the convention with a unit test in the layoutConstants style
A8 must resolve the interaction with the click-origin mark
B1 — the owner gains an explicit rule for the label layer
B2 supersedes batch 2's satellite-play emphasis; the gameActive branch is removed
B2 — via applyCountryBaselinePaint, the single paint owner
B4 invariant — layer-scoped queryRenderedFeatures and ocean-click preconditions
B6 replaces the compare camera mechanism while keeping its behavior contract
C1 — Timezones returns as a real row; consistent with A4/A5
amended coherence rule includes pre-first-interaction idle rotation
F3 — personal bests key per (mode, region) extending the v2 key scheme
F4 — update the existing round-start camera test to 'no move toward the target'
G3 — panelScreenOffset bakes in the collapsed 40vh only
Resolved question 1 — change approved, ships as F4
